messages:
lina: Quick sync — we need a concrete approach for rate limits across endpoints (chat vs embeddings vs rerank vs streaming). Embeddings traffic spikes a lot; chat streaming is latency-sensitive and suffers when bursts occur. Do we go per-endpoint buckets, shared buckets with weights, or hybrid?

jia: My leaning is per-endpoint buckets + a global emergency throttle. Reason: embeddings can blow through a shared bucket and starve chat. Per-endpoint gives predictable SLAs per product surface.

owen: FWIW current impl is one token-bucket per api_key. Moving to per-route will multiply state (N buckets * keys). We need to estimate memory / sync load on the rate-limiter layer. Has anyone profiled at 100k active keys?

kevin: We did a quick sim last quarter (10k keys, 20 routes). Memory overhead was ~1.2MB per 1k keys for bucket state (counters + timestamps). CPU impact was small; biggest pain is coordination when we run the RL in a distributed mode.

rachel: From product: console needs to make these choices visible. Customers will ask "why is embeddings throttled but chat isn't?" We should add per-route quotas in the UI + a simple "burst smoothing" toggle that can be docs-first.

lina: Another operational problem — streaming connection storms: clients open many streaming connections and send a single keep-alive token then quiet. That looks like a short burst but keeps sockets open, causing scaling issues. Proposal sketch: allow a small transient borrow for stream connect (like a burst window) that is reclaimed if not used. Thoughts?

jia: Sketch config example:
```
# per-route token-buckets (example)
routing_rate_limits:
  chat:
    bucket_size_tokens: 1500
    refill_tokens_per_sec: 50
    max_concurrent_streams: 50
    streaming_borrow_window_tokens: 200
  embeddings:
    bucket_size_tokens: 1000
    refill_tokens_per_sec: 20
    allow_burst: true
  rerank:
    bucket_size_tokens: 800
    refill_tokens_per_sec: 10
  global_fallback:
    bucket_size_tokens: 10000
    refill_tokens_per_sec: 200
```

jia: The "streaming_borrow_window_tokens" is what I mean by transient borrow — small credit to let connections land without being immediately rejected. It should be per-connection and decrease quickly.

owen: Concern: that borrow can be gamed. If a client opens N conns, each gets borrow -> spike. We need to limit borrow per-customer per-minute or require auth handshake to consume the borrow. Also enforce a short cooldown per-connection id.

kevin: Alternative: use a sliding window for connection opens (max X opens per Y seconds) instead of token borrow. Might be simpler and less gameable.

rachel: UX: show a "burst history" chart on the endpoint details page and an alert if borrow is being used > threshold. Also expose recommended defaults per tier (free/dev/prod).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled — feature branch for per-route metrics + eviction telemetry to be rolled 03/25 22:00 UTC (will add logs under /metrics/rl/*).

lina: Security note: need to ensure per-endpoint buckets are applied server-side before streaming handshake completes. Otherwise we allow a handshake then apply tokens and close — bad UX. So the decision affects where in the stack we check.

owen: Implementation note: if we keep the limiter as a sidecar we can pre-check and atomically reserve borrow tokens. For distributed limiter (Redis/consul) we need a fast lua script to decrement multiple buckets atomically.

jia: I'm going to write an RFC: per-endpoint buckets + global fallback + streaming borrow window (sliding-window alternative documented) + exploit mitigations (per-conn cooldown, borrow caps). Will include perf numbers and memory cost.

kevin: +1 to RFC. Add a section for token-weighting: count stream-connect as 0.2 tokens until payload arrives, then switch to normal token accounting. That reduces handshake sensitivity.

rachel: Also add console changes + new telemetry widgets to the RFC so product can prioritize the UI work.

lina: Decision request: who okays us to proceed to RFC? Need approval from eng-runtime (+owen), eng-infra (+kevin), and product (+rachel).

owen: I approve pending exact exploit mitigations (lua atomic ops + per-conn cooldown).

kevin: Approve. Please include perf runbook and a toggle gate for canary.

rachel: Approve. Will draft UI mocks after RFC lands.

jia: Cool — I'll open the RFC today and assign owners for benchmarks / console mocks. Action items: 1) Jia write RFC, 2) Owen prototype limiter lua script, 3) Kevin perf sim + mem profiling, 4) Rachel UI mocks, 5) Lina coordinate canary timeline.

lina: Perfect. Thanks team :thumbsup:

kevin: One more tiny ask — let's include a small example snippet in docs on how partners should back off (client-side). Even a 3-line snippet reduces call volume a lot.

rachel: Agreed. We'll include a "recommended client backoff" section in the console docs.

infra-bot: note: tagged ticket RL-412 on the ticket board.

lina: End of thread.
